title: Functions
examples: When should I use a function in my code?
Can a function take more than two inputs?
What is the difference between a parameter and a variable?

explain.say: Today we are learning about functions in coding. A function is like a mini program that performs a specific task.
We use the keyword def to start defining a new function. This tells the computer you are creating something new.
Parameters are the inputs your function needs to work correctly. You list these inside the parentheses when you define it.
The return value is the final result the function gives back when it finishes running. You use the return keyword for this.
Consider a function that calculates the area of a rectangle. It needs length and width as parameters. It returns the calculated area.
In real life, think about a calculator function. When you input two numbers and press equals, the calculator returns the sum. It takes inputs and gives an output.

faq.q: What happens if I forget to return a value?
faq.a: If you forget to return a value, the function will run but will not give back any result to the part of the code that called it. You might get an error or a default null value.
asks: Does the function automatically return something?
What if I just want the function to print something?

faq.q: Can I use the same parameter name in multiple functions?
faq.a: Yes, you can use the same parameter name in different functions. The computer treats each function definition separately, so names do not conflict.
asks: Does Python remember my variable names?

faq.q: Do I have to use every parameter I define?
faq.a: No, you do not have to use every parameter. However, if you define a parameter, the calling code must provide a value for it, or you must give it a default value.
asks: What if I leave a parameter empty?
Can I skip providing an input?

faq.q: What is the difference between printing and returning?
faq.a: Printing displays information to the user on the screen for immediate viewing. Returning passes the actual calculated value back to the program to be used in further calculations.
asks: When should I use print versus return?

faq.q: Can a function return more than one value?
faq.a: Yes, although it looks like one return, Python can return multiple values which are grouped together as a tuple. You can then assign these multiple values to several variables.
asks: How do I get two results from one function?

facts: The 'def' keyword starts the definition of a function.
Parameters act as placeholders for the data the function needs.
The 'return' statement sends the final output of the function.
A function groups reusable blocks of code together.

quiz.say: If a function is defined as calculate(x, y) and you call it with calculate(5, 3), what values are passed as parameters?
quiz.why: The values 5 and 3 are passed directly as the inputs for the parameters x and y.

wrong.1: This is a calculation, not the parameters themselves.
wrong.2: These are the names, not the actual values passed.
wrong.3: This suggests an operation was performed before passing the values.

quiz.say: A function calculates tax on income. If the income is 1000 and the rate is 0.1, what keyword must be used to send the final tax amount back to the main program?
quiz.why: The return keyword is specifically used to send the calculated result back to the caller.

wrong.1: Printing only shows the result on the screen, it does not pass it back for calculation.
wrong.2: Send is not a standard keyword for returning values in this context.
wrong.3: Output is a general term, but 'return' is the precise keyword needed.

quiz.say: Which of these correctly shows the structure for a function named greet that takes one name input?
quiz.why: This structure correctly uses 'def', names the function, and includes one parameter in parentheses.

wrong.1: The colon must follow the parentheses, not the return keyword.
wrong.2: Parameters must be listed inside parentheses.
